proposed_english: to give kingship / to establish as king
rationale: ⲡⲟⲣⲟ as Lycopolitan writing of ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ; the construction ϯ + ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ functions as a verbal idiom 'to make king / give kingship.' Distinct from ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('to be king/reign').

Greek loanword προτομή — technical Manichaean title for the Third Ambassador as the foremost emanation/bust-image of the King of Lights. Retained as Greek-derived term to preserve technical specificity.
Greek πρεσβευτής. The Third Messenger (tertius legatus) of Manichaean cosmology. 'Ambassador' preserves the diplomatic-envoy semantics; 'Messenger' is the more common rendering. Either works.

From verbal root meaning 'to shine forth, to radiate.' Per correspondential translation principle: a divine title from an active-emission verb must preserve the verb quality — 'the Radiance' (active shining-forth), not 'the Splendor' (static quality observed from outside). The Coptic names what the being DOES, not how it looks to an observer.
Confirmed via accumulated vocabulary; the Third Power called by Jesus the Radiance, identified with two faces gazing heavenward.
Verb of uncertain root, possibly cognate with ⲛⲟⲩϥ/ⲛⲏⲩ. Context (Pillar = great Omophoros over all omophoroi) requires a bearing/supporting sense. Tentative.
